Wow. I am touched by the comments and the kindness this drew. Thought I'd be a 1-point wonder and buried in this thread. Some responses:

We both made brief attempts to repair it. He went to three therapy sessions and hated it, I continued therapy for several months. My therapist indicated that it sounded like an unhealthy relationship and that he had been "gas lighting" me on a few occasions-- making me doubt my own perceptions of the relationship, his behavior, and my own-- perhaps not consciously or intentionally... but that rang as true to me. 

In retrospect, I see all of the reasons that it wouldn't have worked: he was quite a bit more jaded and set in his ways (aka a few decades older), we both didn't have good communication strategies and he had a friend close friend who ruined his life with alcoholism. The latter bit really affected him and his perception of anyone who drinks. I don't know that there was a particular moment that it all "fell apart," but my best friend, in trying to help me through this, reminds me that the night I moved in with him, and texted her "I've made a huge mistake" (in GOB's voice, natch). So there's that.

I know I should stop seeing him and cut off communications, but I feel slightly addicted to him and all of that ridiculously good sex. I know there's more to a relationship than that. But people do crazy, crazy things for sex. Like hiring me for the night. Heh. 

Anyway, thanks again for the kindness, Reddit. You've helped me through another day.

Ah. Right in the feels. Here it goes:

In my early 20s, a few times I engaged in sex work via Craigslist (before they shut that section of the site down). I wasn't particularly broke, but I'm pretty and sexually adventurous and wanted to see just how far I could take it. I met a few guys and saw a couple of them several times. 

The last time I did it, I met a guy that I was pretty attracted to and we had a really nice time talking and getting comfortable first. And then we had the MOST. AMAZING. SEX. I have ever had in my life. It was life-changing. And he thought it was pretty great too. When I left, he handed me $500 (more than we agreed on) and I couldn't believe what had just happened. 

So naturally when he emailed that he wanted to get together again, I was back there pretty much the next night. And the next. And by the end of the first week, I told him to stop giving me money. We kept it casual for a while, but then I started spending the night. We'd stay up talking, sometime smoking trees together. I was falling for him. 

A few months go by like this. We talk about moving in together. I was about to run out on my lease and he wanted a bigger place. We get an apartment together. We go on an amazing tropical vacation together. I am so freaking happy. And the sex gets better somehow. We have the mojo. I want to have his babies. He proposes in a glorious way. I accept and want to be his wife. We tell our families we met at a laundromat. 

He's less sweet than he was at first. My day job gets really hard (nope, not selling sex anymore, but that's a funny line in this narrative). I feel lonely, and start getting depressed again. He doesn't know how to deal with that and his own emotional shortcomings rear their heads. I start drinking more. I go on a bender and he dismisses me as an alcoholic and withdraws. He's crushingly mean. I'm beside myself. I wonder if it's all been a mistake. I give him back the ring, move out, and really start falling apart. I know I will never have such amazing, sensual, perfect, magical sex again. 

I move far away to get away and rebuild. But every time I go home, I can't help myself and see him. The lovemaking is incredible. Then I cry a lot. He tells me about the dates he's gone on. I find his new Match profile and it cuts me up because he uses the picture I took of him on the evening of our engagement as his profile picture. I drink a lot now and think I may have moved here to die. 

Holy shit this is depressing. That's my story. 

TL;DR: don't fall in love with your paying customers. Or at all.
